title: [spec-gap][R-06-207] Rust lacks static X25519-from-Ed25519-seed derivation
description:
spec/06-security.md §8.9/§8.7 step 4: 'x25519_private = clamp(SHA-512(ed25519_seed)[0:32])' — clamping per RFC 7748 §5 REQUIRED.

Evidence (sweep 2026-09-01, docs/spec-coverage/06-security-part2.md):
- C: implemented (lichen/subsys/lichen/edhoc/edhoc_crypto.c:287 x25519_keypair_from_seed; documented edhoc_internal.h:89-94); exercised by lichen/tests/edhoc_handshake.
- Python: implemented (python/src/lichen/crypto/identity.py:98-103, :119); used by group_oscore_wrap.py.
- Rust: NOT found anywhere in rust/ — oscore-fork edhoc uses random ephemeral X25519 (initiator.rs:180) and the Ed25519 seed only for signatures (sign.rs:77).

human-only (EDHOC semantics): may be unused-by-design — the fork's METHOD=0 (signature/signature) never uses static DH, so the derivation may be intentionally absent in Rust. Question for mark: add the derivation for parity (spec §8.5 says one keypair unifies everything 'per §8.9'), or amend spec to mark static-DH keys as C/Python-only / optional.
notes: Decision: add for parity. Spec says one keypair unifies everything. Agent-implementable.
